summary: Yu-min Lee is a scholar of Buddhist studies and archaeology who completed graduate studies under John C. Huntington. Lee served as a professor at National Taiwan University (attested 2002).
Yuan Ren works in Sinology and Buddhist studies. Ren earned a PhD at McMaster University (attested 1998) under the supervision of Phyllis Granoff.

Yuanxing Guo (1920–1982) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Gongga Rinpoche and Gangkar Rinpoche. Guo held posts as a researcher at the Buddhist Association of China and at Jinling Scriptural Press.

Yuanying (1878–1953) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under several teachers, including Tongzhi and Bazhi Toutuo. He was abbot of Jiedai, Tiantong, and Yongquan temples, and served as first Venerable Master of the Buddhist Association of China.
Yudru Tsomu is a historian and Tibetologist who earned a PhD at Harvard University under Leonard W. J. van der Kuijp, Mark Elliott, Janet Gyatso, and Philip A. Kuhn.

Yuen Ren Chao (1892–1982) was a linguist and Sinologist who studied at Cornell and Harvard. He held academic posts at Cornell (~1919–1921), Harvard (~1921–1924), Tsinghua University (~1925–1929), and UC Berkeley (~1947–1963).
Yuexia (1858–1917) was a Buddhist studies figure who founded Avatamsaka University, where he also served as a teacher.

Yuguang Liu specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. Liu studied at Northwest Minzu University in 2000 under Samten, Tashi Tsering, Gongbaojie, and Jialuo, and earned a PhD from the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (attested 2005).
Yuhiko Katsuzaki (born 1946) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University (~1965–1974) and later served as its president (~2011–2015).
Yui Chi Lau (1914–1997) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Ying-Kuang Chu and founded the Hong Kong Vajrayana Esoteric Society.

Yui Suzuki specializes in Japanese art history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. Suzuki studied at UCLA under William M. Bodiford, Lothar von Falkenhausen, and Donald F. McCallum, and held a post at the University of Maryland, College Park (attested 2012).

Yuichi Kajiyama (1925–2004) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. Educated at Kyoto University, Nava Nalanda Mahavihara, SOAS, and Vienna, he taught at Kyoto University (1956–1988), Bukkyo University (1988–1997), and Soka University (1997–2001).

Yuishin Ito (1931–2023) was a Buddhist studies and history scholar who studied at Bukkyo and Doshisha universities. He taught at Bukkyo University (1961–1997) and served as president of Kyoto Bunkyo Junior College and Kyoto Bunkyo Gakuen.
Yujiro Motora (1858–1912) was a philosopher who studied at Johns Hopkins University (1885). He held faculty posts at the University of Tokyo (~1888–1912) and the Tokyo University of Education.

Yujun Endo (1928–2017) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. Endo served as an associate professor (attested 1991) and professor emeritus (attested 2014) at Taisho University, and as an advisor at Kawasaki Daishi Research Institute (attested 2014).
Yuka Otani is a scholar in Buddhist studies who held posts as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University and Hanazono University (both attested 2015).

Yukari Kimura specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology, having completed doctoral studies under Kenyo Mitomo. Kimura holds posts affiliated with the Eastern Institute and as a part-time lecturer at Rissho University (attested 2026).

Yukei Matsunaga (1929–2023) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at Koyasan, Tohoku, and Kyushu universities, and held posts at Koyasan University (director, 1983) and Shuchiin University (~1999–2003).

Yuki Sasaki is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who served as a part-time lecturer at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (both attested 2026).

Yukihiko Asayama is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who served as a professor at Hokkaido University of Education (attested 1986) and as an overseas researcher at South China Normal University (attested 1991).
